title: AxisCard
description: The declaration format for a gradient axis (registries/axes/*.axis.json). An axis card DESCRIBES an axis — its semantics, the vocabulary it classifies over, where its source of record lives, and the posture it takes toward absence. It never DUPLICATES the vocabulary: `vocabulary` is a $ref to an enum's $id, and a card that inlines its value list has forked the vocabulary it was meant to point at. Source of truth: this schema; validated by the registries leg of scripts/test-schema.mjs.

axis.description: The axis name; must match the $id suffix and the filename stem.

kind.description: `declared`: the value is authored and stored. `derived`: the value is computed at the evidence-holding edge and never stored as a status column. `two-layer`: a declared floor narrowed by a derived verdict (the reach/vocabulary-split shape).

semantics.description: What this axis means, in prose — including what it is NOT, since axis confusion is the recurring drift.

$ref.description: Pointer to the enum that supplies this axis's values. Never an inline list.

vocabulary.description: The vocabulary this axis classifies over, by reference.

facts.description: Posture of the FACT layer toward absence. Expected `open`: a peer's non-observation is not a negative fact. Declaring `closed` here is a strong claim — it asserts the fact layer is complete — and needs an explicit rationale.

verdicts.description: Posture of the VERDICT layer toward absence. Expected `closed`: absence of a permit is a refusal, never 'unknown, therefore possibly allowed'.

rationale.description: Why each layer takes its posture, grounded in the shipped code that already behaves this way.

closure.description: What silence means on each of this axis's two layers. Required — an axis whose closure posture is undeclared cannot be read by a counterparty that does not share our code.

returns.description: The classifier's return type. For a closed-verdict axis this type must be able to express `refer` — the ceiling marker is never a fallthrough, a timeout, or an error.

gaps.description: Honestly declared distance between this classifier and the law it should satisfy. A named gap is a live obligation, not an excuse.

classifier.description: The total function bridging the open fact layer to the closed verdict layer. REQUIRED when closure.verdicts is `closed`.

ordered.description: Whether the vocabulary carries a meaningful order (mirrors the enum's _ordinal).

values.description: Per-value semantics. The VALUE LIST is owned by the referenced enum; this annotates meaning, it does not define membership.

orthogonalTo.description: Axes this one must not be collapsed into. Axis confusion is the recurring drift; naming the neighbours is how a card resists it.

kind.description: Where this axis's value actually lives. `derived-fold` means it is recomputed, never stored.

sourceOfRecord.description: Where the truth for this axis lives, and how it is reconstructed.

relatedVocabularies.description: Near-miss vocabularies and their dispositions — the drift-check record, kept so the next author does not re-litigate a name collision.

graduation.description: Declared future moves (DNA notarization, persistence tier) — stated, not executed.

allOf.description: Totality law: a closed-verdict axis MUST declare the classifier that bridges its open fact layer to its closed verdict layer.
